Read the passage below, based on the poem 'The Ball Poem', and answer.

"The red kite tugged once, then slipped free of the string and drifted over the rooftops. Meena stood on the terrace with the empty spool in her hand. Her father came up the stairs, saw her face and did not say, 'We will buy another one.' He simply stood beside her, and together they watched the small red shape grow smaller and smaller until the sky had taken it."

Answer the following:
(i) What did Meena lose?  (a) Her bag  (b) Her red kite  (c) Her spool  (d) Her doll
(ii) What does "until the sky had taken it" suggest?  (a) The sky became dark  (b) The kite came back  (c) The kite was gone forever  (d) It started raining
(iii) How is the father like the poet in "The Ball Poem"?
(iv) What feeling does the passage mainly convey?  (a) Quiet sadness  (b) Excitement  (c) Anger  (d) Fear
items.answer: (i) (b) Her red kite (ii) (c) The kite was gone forever (iii) Both choose not to replace the lost object, letting the child learn to bear loss. (iv) (a) Quiet sadness
